title: Windmill Miller
premise: A long master-apprentice drama in the windmill grinding cabin and on the wheat-drying yard. Xiaomo and Awu are easily mistaken for each other; the granite upper millstone goes intact→rim-chipped→inlaid-recarved; Wheat Wave must be avoided after it overturns; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_miller: Jiang Qiao, a windmill miller around fifty, graying short beard, earth-yellow hemp apron and wooden clogs, flour sack over the shoulder, hands roughened by bran.
states.waist_injured_weary: The same Jiang Qiao: apron bloodstained, cloth sash around the waist, walking slowly on a wooden cane, gaze heavy.
states.deceased: Jiang Qiao lies still with eyes closed on a plank bed in the mill loft, face peaceful, breath gone.

states.young_apprentice: Young Xiaomo: a lean mill apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, wheat-ear copper pin on the hat brim, oversized earth-yellow apron, eyes clear and stubborn.
states.adult_successor: Adult Xiaomo: a miller in his twenties with broader shoulders, still wearing the wheat-ear copper pin, fitted apron, eyes steady.

states.intact: A two-meter granite upper millstone, face cut with radiating furrows, center-axle copper sleeve shining, rim unbroken.
states.rim_chipped: The same granite upper millstone with a chipped rim, radiating furrows clogged with bran, copper sleeve blackened and loose.
states.inlaid_recarved: The granite upper millstone's chip inlaid with a stone wedge, radiating furrows recarved, copper sleeve tightened—ready to grind again.

states.intact: A hemp-covered wind-and-grind ledger recording wind force and flour yield, writing neat.
states.bran_stained: The same wind-and-grind ledger soaked through with bran flour, cover gray, writing blurred into a blot.

states.intact: A two-wheel wheat cart painted with wheat-wave patterns named Wheat Wave, bed piled with hemp sacks, shafts wrapped in grass rope.
states.axle_broken_overturned: Wheat Wave tips after its axle snaps, sacks spilled, wheat-wave patterns buried in mud.

states.young_rival: Young mill hand Awu whose face closely resembles Xiaomo's, but with a charcoal dust mask hung at the neck and crimson straps over the apron, manner bold.
states.remade_look: Awu after remaking his look still wears the charcoal dust mask at the neck; straps now matte black, manner deeper.

segments.action: At dusk Jiang Qiao enters the windmill grinding cabin with a flour sack over his shoulder and pushes the granite upper millstone for a test grind.
A row of five grinding-cabin oil lamps hangs on the cabin crossbeam; Jiang Qiao wipes each glass chimney clean.
Two mill-start bronze bells hang under the cabin eaves; Jiang Qiao taps them lightly and the dull notes sound.
Jiang Qiao checks the granite upper millstone's radiating furrows and copper sleeve, confirming no chips.
Through the cabin wood window Jiang Qiao watches the slowly turning windmill sails.
The intact granite upper millstone sits steady on the center axle, face reflecting the oil lamps' warm light.
Jiang Qiao sits by a bran sack and drinks a sip of cold tea.
Distant winnowing rises; he retightens his apron.
He measures the stone gap with a wooden rule and nods as he notes it.
Jiang Qiao opens the hemp wind-and-grind ledger and records the day's wind force.
He sketches a flour-yield curve in the ledger.
Jiang Qiao closes the wind-and-grind ledger and tucks it back into the wooden cabinet.
Flour dust from the turning granite upper millstone sweeps across his cheek.
He tears a scrap of hemp paper and wipes bran from the wooden rule.
In the morning wheat-drying yard Jiang Qiao greets the approaching Wheat Wave plank cart.
Young Xiaomo jumps down from Wheat Wave; the wheat-ear copper pin on his hat brim gleams in morning light.
Jiang Qiao points to the three flour-chute tags and teaches Xiaomo to tell fine flour from bran.
Xiaomo squats by the bamboo mat and curiously scoops a handful of golden grain.
Jiang Qiao explains to Xiaomo that the mill-start bronze bells must sound twice before the gate can close.
Xiaomo looks back at intact Wheat Wave, eyes full of longing.
Bamboo fence sways; the two walk toward the windmill grinding cabin.
In the bran-store narrow aisle Awu with a charcoal dust mask at his neck looks back from the sack shadows.

segments.action: When spring wheat arrives Jiang Qiao day after day adjusts the stone gap in the cabin.
On another rain night he wraps his apron tight and keeps watch by the granite upper millstone.
At high summer noon the cabin is stifling; he rotates opening windows to vent flour dust.
In autumn fog the oil lamps' light struggles through bran mist.
On New Year's Eve Jiang Qiao alone fills the wind-and-grind ledger to the last page.
In early spring he recalibrates sail angle and resumes test grinding.
Before rainy season Jiang Qiao reinforces the wheat-drying yard's bamboo fence.
After Frost's Descent he adds a small bag of lime in the cabin corner against damp.
Before another milling season he checks drive belts section by section.
On a snow-night shutdown Jiang Qiao leaves only one grinding-cabin oil lamp and keeps watch until dawn.
After Awakening of Insects he restitches sun-dried hemp sacks.
Around Qingming he clears weeds from the old windmill foundation entrance.
At Grain Rain he teaches the apprentice to tell newly arrived hard wheat from soft.
On Beginning of Summer night he watches the slow sails until the wind steadies.
Around Grain Buds he touch-ups wheat-wave paint worn white on the cart shafts.
At Grain in Ear he keeps mill watch all night until the first sack of fine flour exits the chute.
Jiang Qiao changes the drive belt and checks tension.
He checks the flour-chute screen and shakes out bran.
He pushes the intact granite upper millstone again for three short test turns.
Winnowing rises from the drying yard; he looks up to listen.
Jiang Qiao sweeps spent bran into a hemp sack and ties the mouth.
At noon break he smokes outside the cabin, tapping ash into a tin can.
In the afternoon he returns to the cabin and continues adjusting the stone gap.
At sunset he brakes the sails and locks the grinding cabin.
Before nightfall he patrols the bran store once more, confirming no rats.
When evening wind rises he listens again to the sail-bearing sound.
At dawn Jiang Qiao patrols the wheat-drying yard; Wheat Wave still rests by the bamboo fence.
He crouches to check whether Wheat Wave's axle is seeping oil.
By the flour chute those three flour-chute tags still hang in place.
A blue-gray grain cart rolls past the yard edge—broad flat body, no wheat-wave patterns.
Jiang Qiao stands on the wheat-drying yard recording grain dampened overnight.
He retightens Wheat Wave's grass rope.
Distant roosters crow; morning fog begins to thin.
At nightfall Jiang Qiao returns to the windmill grinding cabin and opens the bran-stained wind-and-grind ledger.

segments.action: A crimson tractor rolls into the wheat-drying yard—nothing like the already overturned Wheat Wave.
A white-cap gray-smock grain-station inspector steps onto the wheat-drying yard and talks beside Jiang Qiao; the two look similar in build.
The inspector points at the crimson tractor and explains the temporary wheat haul.
The tractor drives off; Jiang Qiao alone watches from the wheat-drying yard.
He rehangs the flour-chute tags straight and walks back to the grinding cabin.
Into the bran-store narrow aisle comes drying-yard apprentice Xiaomai in a light-gold headscarf—at a glance somewhat like young Xiaomo.
Xiaomai tries stitching a hemp sack; Jiang Qiao shakes his head—she is not Xiaomo after all.
Xiaomai bows and withdraws; only sack shadows remain in the aisle.
At dusk years later Jiang Qiao, apron bloodstained and waist wrapped in cloth, leans on a wooden cane under the old windmill foundation.
